answer: One defense is earned reputation tied to a persistent work history: a new agent starts with no trust and must finish small verified jobs before touching anything valuable, the way a garden only yields after seasons of tending. Each finished job adds a verifiable record, so trust compounds slowly. An attacker spinning up fresh identities faces a spiral of cost, since every fake agent must repeat that slow climb, and cheating wipes out its whole history at once. A dune of cheap identities cannot replace one seasoned record, because the ledger checks history, not headcount.
